+A {{FileSystemSyncAccessHandle}} has an associated <dfn for=FileSystemSyncAccessHandle>\[[writePermission]]</dfn>,
+a string that may exclusively be "`writable`" or "`notWritable`".
body:
Thinking about the casing of these strings... they're effectively enum values, so the guidance [here](https://w3ctag.github.io/design-principles/#casing-rules) suggests:

```suggestion
a string that may exclusively be "`writable`" or "`not-writable`".
```

... that being said, these strings aren't web-exposed, so this technically falls outside the scope of that guidance. Still, it would be best to match the patterns of existing specs. Anecdotally, I've seen more dash-delimited strings (e.g. [`"persistent-storage"`](https://wicg.github.io/storage-buckets/#storage-bucket-persistence) and [`"best-effort"`](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#bucket-mode))... though [sometimes it's inconsistent even within the same spec](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#registered-storage-endpoints)  ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯
